entries.title: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS)

edition.value: May 2025 estimates, news release 'Occupational Employment and Wages - May 2025' for release Friday 15 May 2026 (bls.gov/news.release/ocwage.nr0.htm). National file oesm25nat.zip (XLSX).

reference_period.value: May 2025 (a six-panel semiannual sample; the May 2024 notes list panels May 2024 back to November 2021, the May 2025 notes were not read)

licence.name: U.S. Government work, public domain (BLS copyright information page)
licence.commercial_use: not_addressed_by_page (follows from the public-domain statement; confirm for non-US use)
licence.attribution_text: The page asks users to cite BLS as the source (a request, not stated as a condition).
licence.notes: The BLS states its publications are in the public domain except previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations; no permission is needed; the BLS emblem is a registered trademark and its unauthorised use is prohibited. Commercial use is not addressed explicitly: it follows from the public-domain statement (not assessed for use outside the United States).

machine_access.value: Manual download of public XLSX ZIP archives (for example oesm25nat.zip for the national file) and TXT time series; no API key is mentioned on the pages read

update_frequency.value: Annual (May reference period, published the following spring)

geography.value: National, state, metropolitan and nonmetropolitan areas, national industry-specific estimates

classification.value: 2018 SOC, about 830 occupational categories in 22 of 23 major groups (major group 55 military excluded): stated in 'Technical Notes for May 2025 OEWS Estimates' (bls.gov/oes/2025/may/oes_tec.htm). The OEWS tables page and the news release do not state an edition themselves.

limitations: Wages are straight-time GROSS pay exclusive of premium pay; included: base rates, cost-of-living allowances, guaranteed pay, hazardous-duty pay, incentive pay, tips; excluded: overtime, severance, shift differentials, nonproduction bonuses, employer-paid benefits (May 2024 notes).

Annual rates are calculated from hourly rates using a typical 2,080-hour work year for hourly-reported occupations: this derivation is the PUBLISHER's, not a conversion by Ask4Mo, and must be labelled.
Covers employees (full- and part-time); excludes the self-employed, owners and partners of unincorporated firms, household workers and unpaid family workers.
The pages read did not state which statistics (mean, median, percentiles) the files contain or define the O_GROUP field or the suppression symbols: the data dictionary was not read (NOT VERIFIED).
State and metropolitan rows are subnational (policy p10c-e/1 classes them by occupation level and labels them regional).

May 2025 specifics from the May 2025 technical notes: employment is the average of May 2025 and November 2024 QCEW data; the estimates use 2022 NAICS and a model-based (MB3) method with three years of data; a federal funding lapse (1 Oct to 12 Nov 2025) needed extra processing time with no methodology change. Wage definition and the 2,080-hour derivation were read in the May 2024 notes; confirm they are unchanged in the May 2025 notes (the May 2025 page does not restate them in the summary read).

OEWS may publish aggregation or residual codes that are not 6-digit SOC detailed codes: check the data dictionary / O_GROUP values on the actual file before import (NOT VERIFIED: the field layout page was not located).

proposal.evidence_class: C1 (detailed occupations) and C2 (broad groups), by the published occupation group; C1 is not assigned merely because BLS is national
proposal.class_rationale: national official establishment survey with detailed SOC occupations; the level comes from the O_GROUP value, which must be re-read from the source file
proposal.occupation_granularity: SOC 2018 detailed, broad, minor and major groups (O_GROUP, to be verified in the data dictionary)
proposal.geographic_granularity: national (C1/C2); state and metropolitan are regional
proposal.compensation_concept: wage_statistic (straight-time gross wage); pay basis gross per the notes

acquisition.method: manual download of the official national XLSX ZIP (and state/metro files only if regional use is approved) by the owner or an approved operator; record the SHA-256 and the download URL; import through the registry-gated importer after approval
transformations: re-read the national file with the OEWS adapter to capture O_GROUP, percentiles and suppression markers
set soc_edition to 2018 and pay_basis to gross only after the May 2025 technical notes are read
keep annual values as published with the 2,080-hour derivation noted
runtime_dependencies: ESCO or O*NET-SOC crosswalk to link resolver identities
measurement qualification by a named reviewer

entries.title: ONS Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE)
entries.dataset: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE), Table 14 (occupation, four-digit SOC)

edition.value: Employee earnings in the UK: 2025, released 23 October 2025; the 2025 estimates are PROVISIONAL and 2024 estimates are revised. A revised 2025 Table 14 dataset is expected October or November 2026 (the Table 14 page records a correction dated 19 December 2025).

licence.name: Open Government Licence v3.0 (stated on the bulletin and the dataset page: all content under OGL v3.0 except where otherwise stated)
licence.attribution_text: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (the licence's default statement when the provider gives none); the bulletin suggests the citation 'Office for National Statistics (ONS), released 23 October 2025, ONS website, statistical bulletin, Employee earnings in the UK: 2025'.
licence.notes: OGL v3.0 permits commercial and non-commercial use, redistribution and adaptation with attribution; it excludes personal data, third-party rights and logos; the right ends automatically on a breach of the attribution condition. Summary of the licence page, not legal advice.

machine_access.value: Manual download of public XLSX tables from ons.gov.uk dataset pages (the registry records the local Table 14.1a file)

update_frequency.value: Annual (October); provisional then revised the following year

geography.value: United Kingdom (local-authority data for Great Britain in the bulletin)

classification.value: The ASHE 2025 bulletin states 'From 2021, we moved our occupation coding to Standard Occupation Classification 2020 (SOC 2020), from SOC 2010', and its occupation figures are 'as defined by SOC 2020'. The Table 14 dataset page keeps a legacy slug and title naming SOC 2010 and never states SOC 2020. The ASHE 2025 Table 14 file is ashetable142025provisional.zip; its own notes sheet must still confirm the edition before acquisition.

limitations: Medians are the preferred measure; the headline weekly measure is gross weekly earnings for full-time employees (above 30 paid hours; 25 or more for teaching).
Weekly and hourly figures cover employees whose pay for the survey period was not affected by absence; annual figures cover adult-rate employees in the same job for more than one year.
The pay elements included in 'gross' were NOT stated on the pages read (the QMI says hourly earnings exclude overtime): the gross definition is NOT VERIFIED beyond the word gross.
Cells based on fewer than three individuals are suppressed; a dominance rule applies; the coefficient of variation is colour-coded (5%, 10%, 20% thresholds).
ASHE is a 1% sample of PAYE employee jobs; it excludes the self-employed and armed forces; seasonal work is not fully captured.
Weekly pay is published weekly and must stay weekly: no annualisation (decision D-22).

Data correction dated 19 December 2025: annual pay estimates for occupation 3312 (Police officers, sergeant and below) and parent groups 331 and 33 were suppressed in Tables 2, 3, 14, 15 and 20 for UK and some regions; they will be reviewed for the revised 2025 dataset (expected October or November 2026). An import must preserve these as missing, never fill them. The next release date is stated as 'to be announced'.

proposal.evidence_class: C1 (four-digit unit groups) and C2 (one to three digit groups) by the published code length
proposal.class_rationale: national official earnings survey with unit-group detail; the level follows the published code hierarchy, not the publisher's nationality
proposal.occupation_granularity: SOC 2020 unit group (four digits) and broader groups (one to three digits)
proposal.methodology: 1% employer sample from PAYE records, April reference
proposal.population: employees on adult rates, pay unaffected by absence (weekly)
proposal.compensation_concept: wage_statistic (gross weekly pay, median); pay basis gross

acquisition.method: manual download of the Table 14.1a XLSX (preferably the revised 2025 edition once published) by the owner or an approved operator; record SHA-256, URL and the table's own notes; import through the registry-gated importer after approval
transformations: ashe_records with uk_soc_edition 2020 only after the table notes confirm it
keep pay weekly and mark the vintage provisional or revised
reject the row without a native code

suppressed annual-pay cells for occupations 3312, 331 and 33 (UK and affected regions, Tables 2, 3, 14, 15, 20) stay MISSING: never reconstructed, estimated or back-filled from other years or neighbouring groups
weekly pay stays weekly

Medians are the preferred measure; the headline weekly measure is gross weekly earnings for full-time employees (above 30 paid hours; 25 or more for teaching).

ONS publishes a page on classifying SOC 2020 to ISCO-08 and states the full coding index of about 30,000 job titles was recoded to ISCO-08 with the CASCOT tool; the index (Excel) includes ISCO-08 codes and an ISCO-08 structure worksheet (search summary of official pages). A mapping derived from a TITLE index is many-to-many and is not a unit-group equivalence: it would be PARTIAL or AMBIGUOUS, never VERIFIED equivalent.
Weekly and hourly figures cover employees whose pay for the survey period was not affected by absence; annual figures cover adult-rate employees in the same job for more than one year.
